elements.quote: We report interim results of a living systematic review.
elements.reason: The abstract-style summary explicitly identifies the report as a (living) systematic review.

elements.quote: What is the efficacy/effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections?
elements.reason: The abstract states the review question(s) on vaccine efficacy/effectiveness against SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Inclusion/exclusion criteria are described in the methods (text_1) but not in the abstract content.
Information sources and last search date are reported in the main text (text_1, text_3) but not in the abstract.
Risk of bias assessment methods (RoB-2, ROBINS-I) appear in text_2 but not in the abstract.
Methods of presenting/synthesizing results are not described in the abstract content.

elements.quote: We identified a total of 30 studies that investigated VE against symptomatic and/ or asymptomatic infection.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (30) but not the total number of participants or study characteristics.

elements.quote: In fully vaccinated individuals, VE against symptomatic and asymptomatic infections was 80-90% in nearly all studies.
elements.reason: The abstract reports results for the main outcomes (VE against symptomatic/asymptomatic infection).

elements.quote: Due to heterogeneity of study design, time point of analysis, vaccine used, population and settings, we did not perform a meta-analysis.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted, so no summary estimate with CI is required in the abstract.

elements.quote: Fully vaccinated persons are less likely to become infected and contribute to transmission.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates the direction of effect, favoring the vaccinated group.
Limitations of the evidence are discussed in the Discussion (text_7) but not summarized in the abstract.

elements.quote: Fully vaccinated persons are less likely to become infected and contribute to transmission.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their public health implication.
No funding source is stated in the abstract content.
PROSPERO registration (CRD42020208935) appears in the main text (text_1) but not in the abstract.

elements.quote: All vaccines approved by the European Medical Agency (EMA) at the time of writing demonstrated high vaccine efficacy/effectiveness (VE) against severe COVID-19.
elements.reason: The introduction describes the current state of knowledge (high VE against severe disease) and the uncertainty about preventing symptomatic/asymptomatic infection.

elements.quote: With vaccination programmes being implemented in most European countries, it becomes urgent to assess the extent to which these vaccines are also able to prevent symptomatic and asymptomatic infections to guide public health recommendations and develop strategies for fully vaccinated people.
elements.reason: The importance and urgency of the review are explicitly explained in the context of public health needs.

elements.quote: In December 2020, the Robert Koch Institute (RKI)... initiated a living systematic review on the VE and safety of European Union (EU)-licensed COVID-19 vaccines (PROSPERO registration: CRD42020208935).
elements.reason: The manuscript presents itself as a new living systematic review with a PROSPERO-registered protocol; no prior similar systematic review is identified as being updated or replicated, so this conditional element does not apply.
This is a review of intervention effects (COVID-19 vaccines), but no mechanism of action of the vaccines is described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
The review evaluates vaccine efficacy/effectiveness, which is not a complex intervention or complex delivery context; no logic model requirement applies.

elements.quote: In detail, we report the interim results of the review focusing on two research questions: What is the efficacy/effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infections (irrespective
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the review's research questions in the introduction/objectives text, framed around vaccine efficacy/effectiveness against SARS-CoV-2 infection.

elements.quote: We considered studies of any design as long as they had a comparison group that investigated VE against SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection after vaccination with an EMA-approved COVID-19 vaccine (see Supplement Part S2 for complete population intervention comparison outcomes (PICO) questions)
elements.reason: PICO questions are referenced but the complete planned comparisons are deferred to a supplement; only partial PICO elements (population, intervention, comparison implied) are stated in the main text.

elements.quote: We considered studies of any design as long as they had a comparison group that investigated VE against SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection after vaccination with an EMA-approved COVID-19 vaccine (see Supplement Part S2 for complete population intervention comparison outcomes (PICO) questions).
elements.reason: Eligible designs (any design with a comparison group), intervention (EMA-approved COVID-19 vaccines), outcomes, and reference to full PICO questions are specified.

elements.quote: No restrictions were made regarding publication language or status.
elements.reason: Report characteristics (language and publication status) are explicitly addressed; the review period (1 January 2021 to 14 May 2021) is also given.
No evidence distinguishes exclusion of studies because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported; the flowchart only states 'no relevant data (n = 174)'.

elements.quote: we report the interim results of the review focusing on two research questions: What is the efficacy/effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infections (irrespective
elements.reason: Syntheses are grouped by outcome (any SARS-CoV-2 infection vs asymptomatic infection), but explicit grouping of studies (e.g., by vaccine, dose, design) for each synthesis and linkage to PICO comparisons are only partially described in the main text (details deferred to supplements).
No rationale is provided for notable eligibility restrictions such as limiting inclusion to EMA-approved vaccines or studies with comparison groups.

elements.quote: By 14 May 2021 (the date of last search), we identified and screened a total of 4,870 entries.
elements.reason: The date of the last search is explicitly reported (14 May 2021), also stated in text_1 ('The end date of this interim analysis was 14 May 2021') and the PRISMA flowchart caption.

elements.quote: Some of our methodological limitations stem from the rapidly changing publication landscape of COVID-19 vaccine studies. In particular, non-randomised studies on real-world effectiveness are continuously and frequently published on preprint servers. Although we systematically searched seven preprint servers, additional studies could have been published on other servers or websites that we did not capture.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly describes multiple limitations of the review processes, including incomplete preprint coverage, lack of peer review of included preprints, and limited country/vaccine coverage.

elements.quote: Moreover, it has to be considered that these studies did not undergo peer review and should therefore be considered with caution... including the possibility that some studies, in particular those from Israel and the US, might have analysed partly overlapping study populations.

elements.quote: Results of this living systematic review imply that COVID-19 vaccines are highly effective in preventing SARS-CoV-2 infections, including those which are asymptomatic. From a public health perspective, it can be concluded that fully vaccinated persons might in some instances still become PCR-positive for SARSCoV-2 but only play a minor role in the transmission of SARS-CoV-2.
